key_insight: A physics-informed TabPFN model can accurately predict frequency-dependent dielectric spectra of Mo-W-S-Se-Te TMD alloys from sparse ab initio data, including unseen alloy compositions.
engineering_relevance: This enables faster screening and design of tunable 2D optoelectronic materials by reducing reliance on costly first-principles calculations.
method: Generated 99 DFT-calculated alloy structures spanning binary to quinary Mo-W-S-Se-Te compositions.
Used a physics-informed, non-uniform energy subsampling strategy focused on the optically active region above the band gap.
Trained a tabular prior-fitted network (TabPFN) and compared it with Extra Trees and XGBoost baselines.
evidence_signal: Trained only on quaternary alloys, TabPFN achieved R2 > 0.98 and MAE below 0.10 for all four dielectric components on held-out quaternary cases, and reached zero-shot R2 > 0.97 for quinary alloys.
watch_item: Performance depends on the representativeness of the DFT dataset and the chosen energy-sampling scheme, so extrapolation to other TMD chemistries or spectral regimes should be validated carefully.
paper_title: Machine learning based prediction of optical properties in two-dimensional Mo-W-S-Se-Te transition-metal dichalcogenide alloys through physics-informed sampling
